title: control
description: Client -> daemon control frame (~50 Hz). May bundle any subset of jog/action/reset/clutch. seq is for ordering/dedup; send_ms is for latency display only -- neither feeds the safety watchdog.

seq.description: Monotonic per-session counter for ordering/dedup. SHOULD be sent on every motion-bearing frame (jog/action/leader_action_deg). Omitted in practice on reset-only frames by both current clients; the L2 daemon defaults it to -1. Not required, so that real client output validates.

send_ms.description: Client send time (epoch ms). Latency display only.

action_id.description: PROPOSED (Phase E / G1). Correlator for a motion-bearing frame; the daemon echoes it in action_status transitions (accepted->active->done|blocked|clamped|timeout). Optional; ignored if the daemon predates Phase E.

armJog.description:
Per-arm jog rates, keyed by DOF SHORT NAME. Two vocabularies share this object and a robot routes each key by name:

  TASK-SPACE shorts -- "x", "y", "pitch", "shoulder_pan" -- request Cartesian motion. On L2 x/y drive IK(shoulder_lift, elbow_flex), pitch couples wrist_flex, and shoulder_pan orbits the whole arm about the shoulder. On L3 the same keys become a base-frame twist and shoulder_pan yaws the tool about base Z -- a deliberate behaviour change, same wire keys. Note "shoulder_pan" is a task-space VERB here, not a joint: it is not an L3 joint name at all.

  JOINT shorts -- any other key -- drive one joint directly. The legal set is per-robot and MUST be derived from the ack descriptor: strip the "<side>_arm_" prefix and ".pos" suffix from each descriptor.joints entry. L2 accepts its 5-DOF set (shoulder_lift, elbow_flex, wrist_flex, wrist_roll, gripper); L3 accepts its 7-DOF set (shoulder_pitch, shoulder_roll, bicep_yaw, elbow_pitch, forearm_yaw, wrist_pitch, wrist_roll). A client MUST NOT compile in either list.

"gripper" and "wrist_roll" are valid on both. Keys the robot does not recognise are ignored silently, so a typo reads as 'the SDK is broken' -- validate against the descriptor client-side.

base.description:
Base drive intent as normalized rates. The keys are "linear" and "angular" -- NOT the "x.vel"/"theta.vel" names the ack descriptor lists under `base`, which are the telemetry namespace. Sending x/theta here produces an object the robot parses as linear=0, angular=0, i.e. an explicit STOP, with no error.

SIGN CONVENTION (normative): +linear drives the robot FORWARD, +angular turns it LEFT (counter-clockwise, ROS REP-103). No client-side negation. A robot whose hardware turns the other way compensates INTERNALLY, in its own actuator adapter -- never on the wire and never in a shared client. Absence of the `base` object means STOP, not 'hold the last velocity'.

action.description: Absolute lerobot action dict (laptop-side IK path). Keys are <motor>.pos / <axis>.vel in the declared norm_mode.

leaderActionDeg.description: Absolute SO101 leader-arm targets: body joints in DEGREES around the calibrated leader zero; grippers normalized [0,100]. Keys may be <motor> or <motor>.pos. The daemon converts to normalized units via the follower calibration, applies a server-side slew guard (NORI_LEADER_SLEW), then feeds the same TeleopArm P-control/safety path as `action`. Applied after `action` when both are present (leader wins on shared keys).

clutch.description: VR squeeze-to-move (M2). When false, the laptop mapper emits zero jog.
